extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS attendees and the ML research community
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement of NeurIPS 2022 Outstanding Papers, Outstanding Datasets & Benchmarks Papers, and Test of Time Award. Each winning paper carries a one-paragraph selection-committee rationale describing the underlying paper-quality property being praised (theoretical depth, practical impact, framework openness, insight, novelty, well-thought-out survey, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical study with concrete impossibility theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: This work provides a theoretical study of out-of-distribution (OOD) detection, focusing on the conditions under which such models are learnable. The work uses probably approximately correct (PAC) learning theory to show that OOD detection models are PAC learnable only for some conditions of the space of data distributions and the space of prediction models. It provides 3 concrete impossibility theorems, which can be easily applied to determine the feasibility of OOD detection in practical settings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (Is Out-of-distribution Detection Learnable?). Praised attributes: principled use of PAC theory, concrete theorems with practical applicability, and a theoretical grounding for existing empirical approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opens new theoretical questions
rubrics_metrics.description: This work also raises new theoretical questions, for example, about the learnability of near-OOD detection. As such, it has the potential for broad theoretical and practical impact in this important research area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generative potential for future work cited as a quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-of-the-art results with effective architectural decoupling
rubrics_metrics.description: This work represents one of the state of the art of such models, but also innovates in demonstrating the effective combination of an independently trained large language model with an image decoder at scale. This inherently practical decoupling is likely to be a dominant paradigm for large scale text to image models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (Photorealistic Text-to-Image Diffusion Models with Deep Language Understanding / Imagen). Praised for SOTA performance, an architectural innovation (decoupling LLM from decoder), and forecasted long-term paradigm influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impressive results with broad audience interest
rubrics_metrics.description: The results are impressive and of interest to a broad audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct quote from the Imagen rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-thought-through survey that organises prior work into a coherent framework
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper is an excellent demonstration of how a well thought through survey, that seeks not just to list but to organise prior research into a coherent common framework, can provide insights that then lead to new modelling improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (Elucidating the Design Space of Diffusion-Based Generative Models). Praised for moving beyond enumeration to synthesis and for yielding new modelling improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likely lasting contribution to understanding and implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper is likely to be an important contribution in the evolution of both the understanding and implementation of Diffusion Process based models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward-looking impact attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framework enabling scaling and broad applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: This work provides a framework for training embodied AI agents on large quantities of data, creating the potential for such agents to benefit from scaling, as language and image generation models have. The core of the framework is an engine for building procedurally-generated, physics-enabled environments with which agents can interact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (ProcTHOR). Cited qualities: scalable framework, combinatorial diversity of environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-source release as a valuable community asset
rubrics_metrics.description: The framework and code used in this work will be open-sourced, providing a valuable asset for the research community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open-source release explicitly cited as part of the contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clean approach that combines complementary signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-training on program abstractions and natural language enables incorporating human biases into learning. This is a clean approach to incorporating human biases but also be robust with program abstractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (Using natural language and program abstractions to instill human inductive biases in machines). Praised for cleanliness and robustness of the technical approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Departure from a dominant paradigm with gradient-based optimization benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: It joins a small but growing line of research that departs from the dominant high recall-sparse retrieval paradigm. Notably, this new paradigm allows for gradient-based optimization of the indexer for target applications using standard deep learning algorithms and frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (A Neural Corpus Indexer for Document Retrieval). Cited qualities: paradigm-shifting, integrable with standard deep learning workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant empirical improvement with documented limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed approach introduces architectural and training choices that result in significant improvements compared to prior work, demonstrating the promise of neural indexers as a viable alternative. The paper is well-written and discusses the limitations and open questions following from this work, which can serve as inspiration for future research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised for being well-written and for transparent discussion of limitations and open questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical insight into nonconvex optimization through scaling limits
rubrics_metrics.description: This work studies the scaling limits of SGD with constant step-size in the high-dimensional regime. It shows how complex SGD can be if the step size is large. Characterizing the nature of SDE and comparing it to the ODE when the step size is small gives insights into the nonconvex optimization landscape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (High-dimensional limit theorems for SGD). Praised for yielding insights into the nonconvex optimization landscape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ubiquitous applicability and large potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper reduces sensitivity to hyperparameters in gradient descent by developing a method to optimize with respect to hyperparameters and recursively optimize *hyper*-hyperparameters. Since gradient descent is everywhere, the potential impact is tremendous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (Gradient Descent: The Ultimate Optimizer). Cited for breadth of applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novel and technically useful generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper generalizes score-based generative model (SGM) from Euclidean space to Riemannian manifolds by identifying major components that contribute to the success of SGMs. The method is both a novel and technically useful contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (Riemannian Score-Based Generative Modelling).

rubrics_metrics.name: New interpretation of a classical tool with practical improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper considers gradient estimation when the distribution is discrete. Most common gradient estimators suffer from excessive variance. To improve the quality of gradient estimation, they introduce a variance reduction technique based on Stein operators for discrete distributions. Even though Stein operator is classical, this work provides a nice interpretation of it for gradient estimation and also shows practical improvement in experiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (Gradient Estimation with Discrete Stein Operators). Praised for combining a fresh interpretation with empirical improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model-prediction-experiment cycle leading to practical artifact
rubrics_metrics.description: The work asks 'Given a fixed FLOPs budget, how should one trade-off model size and the number of training tokens?'. The work models this trade off, makes a prediction based on this model, and trains a model corresponding to that prediction. The resultant model, that is significantly smaller but is trained on significantly more tokens, outperforms its counterpart, while also being more practical to use downstream due to its smaller size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (Chinchilla scaling laws). Praised for end-to-end methodology: theory -> prediction -> experimental confirmation -> practical artifact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reshapes community thinking about an important problem
rubrics_metrics.description: All in all, this work sheds new light on the way the community thinks about scale in the context of language models, which may be useful in other domains of AI as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward-looking community-impact attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renews focus on a neglected dimension via theory + empirics
rubrics_metrics.description: This work renews our focus on the importance of selecting high quality data as a means to achieve optimal scaling. It does so through a nicely designed analytic investigation that develops a theoretical model of the impact of data quality in concert with empirical instantiation of a range of data filtering metrics on ImageNet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (Beyond neural scaling laws). Praised for combining a theoretical model with careful empirical instantiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insightful, timely, and debate-shaping
rubrics_metrics.description: This work is both insightful and timely and will shape the debate about the tradeoffs in the many dimensions of scale in machine learning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forward-looking attribution of intellectual influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Near-optimal theoretical results for an important problem class
rubrics_metrics.description: This paper studies multiple distribution learning using techniques from stochastic zero-sum games. This technique leads to very interesting theoretical results for a class of problems with near optimal results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding Paper (On-Demand Sampling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratizing access to large-scale data for the broader community
rubrics_metrics.description: Until now, no datasets of this size have been made openly available for the broader research community. This work presents LAION-5B, a dataset consisting of 5.85 billion CLIP-filtered image-text pairs, aimed at democratizing research on large-scale multi-modal models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding D&B Paper (LAION-5B). Praised for democratization through open release of an unprecedented-scale dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrated utility by reproducing foundational models
rubrics_metrics.description: Moreover, the authors use this data to successfully replicate foundational models such as CLIP, GLIDE and Stable Diffusion, provide several nearest neighbor indices, as well as an improved web-interface, and detection scores for watermark, NSFW, and toxic content detection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised for proving the dataset's utility by replicating foundational models, providing auxiliary tools (indices, web interface), and shipping safety-relevant detection scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framework supporting open-ended task generalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Autonomous agents have made great strides in specialist domains like Atari games and Go, but typically fail to generalize across a wide spectrum of tasks and capabilities. This work introduces MineDojo, a new framework built on the popular Minecraft game that features a simulation suite with thousands of diverse open-ended tasks and an internet-scale knowledge base with Minecraft videos, tutorials, wiki pages, and forum discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awarded Outstanding D&B Paper (MineDojo). Praised for addressing a clear research gap (specialist vs. generalist agents) with a framework spanning simulation + knowledge base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open release of simulation, knowledge bases, algorithm, and pretrained models
rubrics_metrics.description: It also proposes a novel agent learning algorithm that is able to solve a variety of open-ended tasks specified in free-form language. It provides an open-source simulation suite, knowledge bases, algorithm implementation, and pretrained models to promote research on generally capable embodied agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praised for full open-source ecosystem release (simulator + knowledge + algorithm + pretrained models).

rubrics_metrics.name: Huge, paradigm-shifting community impact (Test of Time)
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2012, it was presented as the first CNN trained on the ImageNet Challenge, far surpassing the state-of-the-art at the time, and since then it has made a huge impact on the machine learning community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test of Time Award rationale for AlexNet.
